title: Maximum Sum of Distinct Subarrays With Length K
statement: You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. Consider every contiguous block of exactly `k` elements of `nums` in which no value appears twice. Return the largest sum among those blocks, or `0` if no block of length `k` has all distinct values.
notes:
## Intuition

Summing every block of length `k` from scratch and checking it for repeats costs O(n·k). Neighbouring blocks share all but two elements: one value enters on the right and one leaves on the left. Keeping a running sum and a count of each value inside the window updates both in O(1) per step. The window has `k` distinct values exactly when the count map holds `k` keys.

## Approach

1. Keep `counts` (value to how many times it is in the window), `windowSum`, and `best = 0`.
2. Move `right` across `nums`. Add `nums[right]` to `windowSum` and to `counts`.
3. Once `right >= k`, the value `leaving = nums[right - k]` drops out: subtract it from `windowSum`, lower its count, and delete the key when the count hits 0.
4. If `counts.size === k`, the window is full and has no repeats, so update `best`.
5. Return `best` (still 0 if no window qualified).

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 5, 4, 2, 9, 9, 9]`, `k = 3`.

- `right = 2`: window `[1, 5, 4]`, 3 keys, `best = 10`.
- `right = 3`: 1 leaves, window `[5, 4, 2]`, `best = 11`.
- `right = 4`: 5 leaves, window `[4, 2, 9]`, `best = 15`.
- `right = 5`: window `[2, 9, 9]` has only 2 keys, skipped.
- `right = 6`: window `[9, 9, 9]` has 1 key, skipped. The answer is `15`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index enters and leaves the window once.
- Space: O(k): the map holds at most `k` keys.

## Pitfalls

- Delete a key when its count reaches 0; otherwise `counts.size` overcounts distinct values.
- Remove the leaving value before testing the window, or the window briefly holds `k + 1` elements.
- On LeetCode the sum can reach about 10^10, so Java and C need a 64-bit `long`.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `counts` | value to number of times it occurs in the window |
| `windowSum` | sum of the current window |
| `best` | largest sum of a valid window so far |
| `right` | index of the newest element in the window |
| `leaving` | the value that just slid out on the left |
